data.long_meaning: The name Allene is derived from the Old English words ‘eal’ meaning ‘entire’ and ‘leon’ meaning ‘lion’. In its entirety, Allene means ‘entire lioness’ or ‘radiant one’. This name is believed to have been used in England during the Middle Ages and was popularized by the poet Geoffrey Chaucer in his work ‘The Canterbury Tales’.

It is associated with the biblical name 'Allan', which is found in the book of Ruth (Ruth 1:2). In Christian tradition, Allene represents beauty, grace, and elegance. People with this name are often characterized as being elegant, refined, and possessing a touch of sophistication. Allene is also associated with the Latin words 'pulchra' and 'forma', meaning 'beautiful form' or 'lovely appearance'. In modern usage, Allene is a variant of the name 'Allene', which is commonly used in Christian cultures.
